chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me who said: Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to me, from Abdul Aziz ibn Umar al-Wasiti, from Abu Khalid al-Sijistani, from Yazid ibn Khalid al-Neishaboory, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Friendship has certain boundaries/conditions. Whoever does not possess these boundaries, do not attribute to him the perfection of friendship. And whoever does not possess any of these boundaries, do not attribute to him [anything of] friendship. The first is that his secret and his public self are one for you. The second is that he considers your beauty/goodness as his own, and your ugliness/badness as his own. The third is that wealth or position does not change him. The fourth is that he does not withhold from you anything that his capability reaches. And the fifth is that he does not leave you alone at times of calamity/hardship.
ai.seo_question: What are the five conditions of true friendship according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) five criteria for true friendship, emphasizing that sincerity requires consistency between a friend's inner and outer selves, shared perception of virtues and flaws, and immunity to the corrupting influence of wealth or status. This tradition highlights the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) and *wafa'* (steadfastness), where a true friend remains loyal during hardships and generous within their means, reflecting the spiritual bond of *wilayah*.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-19 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masruq al-Nehdi quoted Abdul Aziz ibn Umar al-Vaseti, on the authority of Abi Khalid al-Sejestani, on the authority of Yazid ibn Khalid al-Neishaboory that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“Friendship has certain conditions. Do not consider one who doesn’t have these conditions to be your perfect friend. Whoever doesn’t have any of these conditions has no basis for being your friend. The first condition is that he should be so honest with you that his hidden personality and his evident personality are the same for you. The second condition is that he should consider your good name as his own good name and your badness as his own badness. The third condition is that he should not change when he gets some wealth or a position. The fourth condition is that he should not withhold from you what he can. And the fifth condition is that he should not leave you alone at times of hardship.”
